newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela cabinet oks Arco/Corpoven heavy oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela cabinet oks Arco/Corpoven heavy oil deal.

text.p: The Venezuelan cabinet on Wednesday approved a joint venture worth some $3.5 billion between Atlantic Richfield Co and Lagoven, a unit of Venezuela's state-owned oil company PdVSA, Ministers said.

Minister of Information Fernando Egana told reporters the project -- which still requires congressional approval -- would boost Venezuelan gross domestic product (GDP) by between 0.2 to 0.3 percent per year.
Egana hoped approval would be forthcoming "before congress breaks for the year" in mid-December.
Under the joint venture, the companies will work together to produce up to 200,000 barrels per day of nine-degree API extra-heavy crude oil from the Hamaca zone in Venezuela's Orinoco tar belt.

The project will have three phases, including construction of a pipeline and an upgrading unit on the Caribbean coast at San Jose, north of the field, by 2001. By 2006, the joint venture will be converting 180,000 bpd of heavy crude into 25-degree API crude, similar in quality to Alaskan North Slope Crude, the companies have said.
